content.title: About
content.content: Nectarines are juicy fruits of the nectarine tree (Prunus persica var. nucipersica), closely related to peaches but without the fuzzy skin. Grown in warm regions worldwide, they have a sweet aroma and a mildly tart flavor. Nectarines can be eaten raw, used in cooking, baking, desserts, and juices.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Nectarines and peaches belong to the same species; the difference is the smooth skin of nectarines.
Nectarines contain more vitamin C than most berries.
In Japan, nectarines are a symbol of longevity and are often served at celebratory meals.
Nectarine seeds contain amygdalin, which can release cyanide when processed.
Nectarines may be green, yellow, or red depending on the cultivar.

items.title: Rich in vitamin C
items.content: Vitamin C supports the immune system and aids collagen synthesis.

items.title: Source of dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber improves digestion and helps maintain satiety.

items.title: Contains potassium
items.content: Potassium contributes to normal heart function and blood pressure regulation.

items.title: Contains antioxidants
items.content: Flavonoids and carotenoids protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Low in calories
items.content: Nectarines provide energy while being relatively low in calories, making them suitable for weight‑management diets.

items.title: Allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to nectarines.

items.title: Cyanogenic compounds in the pit
items.content: The pit should not be swallowed, as it can release cyanide when broken down.

items.title: Pesticide residues
items.content: When buying non‑organic fruit, wash thoroughly to reduce pesticide exposure.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Nectarines can be eaten fresh, sliced into salads, added to smoothies, baked in pies, or used to make sauces. The skin is edible and adds extra nutrients, though it can be peeled if preferred.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store nectarines in the refrigerator at 0‑4 °C in a plastic bag or container. At room temperature they keep for 2‑3 days but quickly lose aroma and softness.
